raw_case_text:
He was a son of 29-year-old mother, second gesture, second pare, and a 35-year-old father, both parents were without any medical surgical antecedents or family defects. He is the oldest of two siblings, the second is 13-month-old and in good health.
The patient lives in Thiaroye district, in the suburbs of Dakar, characterized by insalubrity with stagnant water, swampy areas, and domestic animals roaming around. This particular biotope is favourable for the circulation of the Phlebotomus insects, vectors of Leishmania species. In the household, all family members slept under impregnated mosquito nets, and prior to admission, the patient had not travelled outside the residence area.
He was admitted to the Paediatric Department of the Pikine National Teaching Hospital on November 25th, 2019, for a worsening of epistaxis and gingivorrhagia that had been manifesting sporadically for 3 months without any real follow-up.
At admission, the patient had fever with a body temperature at 39.5 C, a heart rate of 153 btt/min, respiratory rate of 48 c/min, and capillary blood glucose of 1.3 g/L. Blood pressure was normal at 93/62 mmHg, and arterial oxygen saturation was 97%. Weight and height were 12 kg and 97 cm, respectively, with a ratio of weight/height at -2 SD and brachial perimeter at 13 cm.
Clinical examination revealed haemorrhagic syndrome with bilateral epistaxis of great abundance with clotting, severe anaemic syndrome that was poorly tolerated, moderate respiratory distress syndrome, and systemic inflammatory response syndrome with fever at 39.5 C. A tumor syndrome with hepatomegaly of 11 cm, 12 cm splenomegaly type IV of the Hackett classification, and noninflammatory macropoly adenopathies in the cervical and axillary areas were noted. In addition, there were multiple mouth ulcers. Examination of the other organs was unremarkable. A chest X-ray had revealed bilateral pneumonia, and abdominal ultrasound, apart from objectified hepatosplenomegaly, was normal.
The diagnosis of malignant haemopathy was evoked with blood count which showed hypochromic microcytic anaemia (3.44%/79500) with a haemoglobin level at 05.1 g/dl and severe thrombocytopenia at 3000/mm3. However, the smear was not in concordance with level of 7% blasts and 3% erythroblasts.
Faced with this infectious syndrome, we looked for and eliminated malaria, retrovirosis, hepatitis, and severe sepsis picture in a particular field such as sickle cell disease or vitamin B9 or B12 deficiency.
Thus, the diagnosis of visceral leishmaniasis was evoked based on clinical symptoms such as tumor syndrome with splenomegaly and adenopathy. We collected a lymph node biopsy for microscopy examination; however, the results were negative. As other probable conditions were formally ruled out, bone marrow aspiration was performed for diagnosis.
The biological sample was sent to the Parasitology-Mycology Reference Laboratory at the Faculty of Medicine, Cheikh Anta Diop University of Dakar, for microscopy and molecular diagnostic. For microscopy identification, direct examination of the spinal cord cytopic fluids after GIEMSA staining revealed amastigote forms of Leishmania (Figure 1).
For molecular diagnostic, parasite DNA was extracted from collected blood samples by QIAmp DNA blood mini kits, following the manufacturers' protocol. Extracted DNA was amplified in 96-well PCR microplates by the CFX96 qPCR machine. For the outer PCR primers, CSB2XF (C/GA/GTA/GCAGAAAC/TCCCGTTCA) and CSB1XR (ATTTTTCG/CGA/TTTT/CGCAGAACG) were used. The 30 microL of outer PCR mixture consisted of the CSB2XF/CSB1XR (1 microM/primer) and 1.0X TEMPase Hot Start Master Mix (including 3.0 mM MgCl2, 0.4 mM dNTPs, and 0.2 units/microl TEMPase Hot Start DNA Polymerase) and 1 microL of extracted DNA. The reaction mixture of the nested PCR was identical to that of the outer PCR, and the primer sets 13Z (ACTGGGGGTTGGTGTAA AATAG) and LiR (TCGCAGAACGCCCCT) were used. Positive and negative controls were included during the PCR. The nested PCR products were confirmed by running the controls by electrophoresis on a 1.5% agarose gel. PCR performed on December 19, 2019, on extracted DNA from bone marrow showed that Leishmania infantum was the responsible species.

subjective.chief_complaint: A pediatric male patient (height 97 cm, weight 12 kg; older brother of a 13-month-old sibling) was admitted on November 25, 2019, for worsening epistaxis and gingivorrhagia evolving sporadically over 3 months.
subjective.history_of_present_illness: The child experienced sporadic epistaxis and gingival bleeding for 3 months without regular medical follow-up, which acutely worsened and prompted admission to the Paediatric Department of Pikine National Teaching Hospital.
subjective.past_medical_history: Born to a 29-year-old G2P2 mother and 35-year-old father without medical, surgical, or familial disorders; healthy 13-month-old younger sibling. Resided in Thiaroye district (suburbs of Dakar, Senegal), an area with stagnant water, swamps, and roaming domestic animals favorable for Phlebotomus vectors; slept under impregnated mosquito nets with no travel outside the district.
subjective.review_of_systems: Positive for fever, abundant bilateral epistaxis, gingivorrhagia, oral ulcers, and dyspnea.

objective.physical_examination: Temperature 39.5 C, heart rate 153 bpm, respiratory rate 48 breaths/min, blood pressure 93/62 mmHg, SpO2 97%, weight 12 kg, height 97 cm (weight-for-height -2 SD), mid-upper arm circumference 13 cm. Exam showed severe poorly tolerated pallor/anemia, abundant bilateral epistaxis with clots, gingivorrhagia, multiple oral ulcers, moderate respiratory distress, systemic inflammatory response syndrome, hepatomegaly (11 cm), Hackett grade IV splenomegaly (12 cm), and non-inflammatory cervical and axillary macro-polyadenopathy.
objective.routine_investigations: Capillary blood glucose was 1.3 g/L. CBC revealed severe hypochromic microcytic anemia (Hb 5.1 g/dL) and profound thrombocytopenia (platelets 3,000/mm3), with 7% blasts and 3% erythroblasts on peripheral smear. Workup for malaria, HIV/retrovirus, viral hepatitis, bacterial sepsis, sickle cell disease, and vitamin B9/B12 deficiency was negative. Chest X-ray showed bilateral pneumonia; abdominal ultrasound confirmed hepatosplenomegaly without other abnormalities.
objective.advanced_workup: Lymph node biopsy microscopy was negative for parasites. Bone marrow aspiration cytopathology stained with Giemsa revealed Leishmania amastigotes.

assessment_and_plan.assessment_and_confirmation: Hematologic malignancy, malaria, HIV, viral hepatitis, and vitamin deficiencies were excluded. Direct microscopy of Giemsa-stained bone marrow aspirate identified Leishmania amastigotes, and nested PCR (outer primers CSB2XF/CSB1XR; inner primers 13Z/LiR) on bone marrow DNA confirmed Leishmania infantum as the causative agent of Visceral Leishmaniasis.
